I was very worried all night.
I did not sleep at all today.

Report any problems to me immediately.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Denis.
Hi, Katya.

examples.text: Добрый день! Рады приветствовать вас в нашем отеле.
examples.trans: Good afternoon! We are glad to welcome you to our hotel.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что ты забыл на моей кухне?
examples.trans: What did you lose in my kitchen?

examples.text: Миша, иди ты в свой кабинет.
examples.trans: Misha, go to your own office.
You were upset because of yesterday.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.text: В моём отеле должен быть идеальный порядок!
examples.trans: There must be ideal order in my hotel!
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'строенный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('upset').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень расстроенный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very upset choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто расстроенный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply upset day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You were upset because of yesterday.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('yesterday's').

examples.trans: You were upset because of yesterday.
Yesterday's grand opening was a total failure.

examples.text: Ты что здесь делаешь? После вчерашнего!
examples.trans: What are you doing here? After yesterday!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In a hotel there are always breakfasts.
Come on, wake up faster.

examples.text: На моей кухне всегда идеальный порядок!
examples.trans: There is always ideal order in my kitchen!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Миша, иди ты в свой кабинет.
examples.trans: Misha, go to your own office.
No, everything is fine.

examples.text: Я должен рассказать Кате или нет?
examples.trans: Should I tell Katya or not?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All our management will be there.
No, everything is fine.
Calm down, everything is fine.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: No, everything is fine.
Calm down, everything is fine.
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, please.

examples.text: Я знаю, что ты этого не простишь.
examples.trans: I know that you will not forgive this.

examples.text: Даже если простишь, то никогда не забудешь.
examples.trans: Even if you forgive, you will never forget it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?
The cooks have to get up early.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Forgive me, please.
Please do not tell them anything.
Here you go, here is your finest coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'entire', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: My conscience is still bothering me anyway.
And where did all the coffee go?
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'night' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I was very worried all night.

examples.text: Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
examples.trans: I did not sleep all night either.
I tossed and turned all night long.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто-то не хочет вставать с кровати.
examples.trans: Someone does not want to get out of bed.
I was very worried all night.
Everyone listen to me very carefully!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'живать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'I was worried', paired with 'пережить'.

examples.trans: I was very worried all night.
Why are you worrying like that?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: I did not sleep at all today.

examples.text: Ты что, совсем с ума сошёл?
examples.trans: Have you completely lost your mind?
Are you a complete fool?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: I will eat at work today.

examples.text: Тайный гость будет сегодня или завтра.
examples.trans: The secret guest will be here today or tomorrow.
Be on alert today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Гости ресторана — это не только посетители.
examples.trans: Restaurant guests are not just casual visitors.

examples.text: Кто-то не хочет вставать с кровати.
examples.trans: Someone does not want to get out of bed.

examples.text: Утренняя смена на кухне уже началась!
examples.trans: The morning shift in the kitchen has already started!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'slept', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.trans: I did not sleep at all today.

examples.text: Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
examples.trans: I did not sleep all night either.
It is clear why you did not get enough sleep.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
examples.trans: I did not sleep all night either.
Very nice to meet you too.
Me too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'рочаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'tossed and turned'.

related.gloss: not to tossed and turned (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и ворочаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and tossed and turned on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют ворочаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to tossed and turned.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.

examples.text: Гости ресторана — это не только посетители.
examples.trans: Restaurant guests are not just casual visitors.
They are also hotel residents.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is clear why you did not get enough sleep.
I hope Katya will be able to understand me.
All clear.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что ты забыл на моей кухне?
examples.trans: What did you lose in my kitchen?

examples.text: Если что-то не так, персонал штрафуют.
examples.trans: If something goes wrong, they fine the staff.
What is happening over there right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'спаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got enough sleep'.

examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich needs to sleep well.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и выспаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and got enough sleep on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.
Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
examples.trans: Report any problems to me immediately.

examples.text: Не люблю, когда мясо плохо прожарено.
examples.trans: I do not like it when the meat is poorly cooked.
Any time.

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.trans: Mikhail, there is a small problem there.

examples.text: О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
examples.trans: Report any problems to me immediately.
He is solving problems with suppliers.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.text: О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
examples.trans: Report any problems to me immediately.
The fire alarm went off up there.
Better tell her everything right away.

meanings.en: to inform, to report, to announce (+ dat.)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ообщать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to report / inform', paired with 'сообщить'.

examples.text: О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
examples.trans: Report any problems to me immediately.

examples.text: Мы с радостью сообщаем вам новость.
examples.trans: We gladly inform you of the news.
The newspapers report on the election.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.
Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
examples.trans: And here is the owner of our hotel.

examples.text: Виктория Сергеевна, я тут вот что подумал.
examples.trans: Victoria Sergeevna, here is what I just thought.
No, here it is, this one is mine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.
Our restaurant is located right here.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'owner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
examples.trans: And here is the owner of our hotel.
I am the owner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.
Our restaurant is located right here.
A bit faster, well, where is our bacon?

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Before you is our new hotel.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I did not come here to get acquainted.
Do not hesitate, come right in here.
Give me the keys.

meanings.en: to get acquainted, to meet (someone new)
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get acquainted', paired with 'познакомиться'.

examples.trans: I did not come here to get acquainted.
Very nice to meet you, Denis.
Well then, let's get acquainted.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'came', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.
I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Everyone listen to me very carefully!
In short, listen to my new advice.
Listen, Denis, I will try.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Everyone listen to me very carefully!
Read everything carefully!
Listen to the teacher attentively.
